main_text.p: {a}gentilibus quidem pepercerat: quos de-a gentibus aut ethnicis.ferere inveteratas superstitiones,&ad unum ritu deducere tentaverat){b}illisb Iudæis quidem,{c} ubi nihil sancti erat, facile relinquētibus:c Antiochū apud sed tamen omnibus metu ac clade affectis, vectigalia cessaverant.quæ nihil sancti erat [?] Quibus rebus æstuans (etenim ipse olim omnibus regibus opulentior, suomet ícelere inopiam perferat) copias cum Lysia partitur, eiq; Syriam & bellum adversus Iudæos committit, ipse in Persas ad cogēda vectigalia profectus. Igitur Lysias duces belli delegit, Ptolemæum, Gorgiam, {d}Doronem,delenda videtur. & Nicanorem: his quadraginta millia pedi-tum, septem equitum data. Ac primo impetu magnum Iudæis terrorem intulerūt. Tum Iudas cūctis desperantibus suos ad-Tertia expeditio Iudæ.hortatus, forti animo descēderent in præ-lium: Deo fretis, nihil invictum fore. Sæpe antea a paucioribus adversum plures{e} be-e.1.feliciter.ne pugnatum. Iejunio indicto, celebratoque sacrificio, in aciem descensum, fusæhæc in Maspha acciderunt. hostium copiæ: Iudas castris potitus, mul-i.Mac.3.tumque ibi auri & Tyriarum opum repertum. Namque ex Syria negociatores nihil de victoria dubitantes, regium exercitum sequuti, spe captivos mercandi, prædæ

page.notes: Reference marks a–e are printed in the text; their notes are placed beside the lines where the marks stand. The note on "quæ nihil sancti erat" is hard to read and its placement is uncertain. "celebratoque" is printed as "celebrato" with a mark at the line end, and I read it as one word. "mul." is followed by a stop before "tumque", and "i.Mac.3." sits beside it, so the word division is uncertain. The "ad-" and "præ-" line-end hyphens are read from the scan. The "Antiochū" note is printed in broken type and the reading is uncertain.
